item.title: Spectral completeness of the declared PEC waveguide and cavity classes
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers. Let the PEC classes be those of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. Then:
(a) **Smooth cavity.** The curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace that is retained; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally with the PEC trace. The associated second-order wave with initial displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$ has coefficients $a_j''+c^2\lambda_ja_j=0$, converges in $C_tV\cap C_tH$ for finite-energy data, and retains the finitely many $\lambda=0$ modes $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The classical smoothness of the eigenfields on the declared smooth domain, and the solvability of the shifted auxiliary boundary problems used in the construction, are those supplied by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] on $\Omega$.
(b) **Rectangular class.** For a rectangular box the separable products described in the mode verification are dense in the reflection-parity energy class, and every initial datum of that class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class with constant energy, with finite separated modes dense at every time. The rectangular statements are the recorded rectangular reflection-class completeness lemma [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (the $G2$ branch); the individual TE/TM mode verification against the Maxwell equations and the PEC conditions is the recorded $G1$ physics branch, homed on the physical guide page and not consumed here as a mathematical premise. No completeness in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes is asserted.
item.strategy: The smooth-cavity assertions are exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]], whose proof constructs the compact self-adjoint solution operator of the shifted problem with the coercive solver and the smooth-domain interior estimate, applies the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem to obtain the eigenbasis and the multiplicities, and derives the distributional eigen-equation and the modal wave expansion with zero modes retained. This item records the composition with the elliptic existence theorem of this page: [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] supplies the weak solvability and the classical ($C^\infty$-on-the-closure) upgrade on the bounded smooth domain for the elliptic boundary problems used in the closure argument, so the eigenfields and the auxiliary problems live on the declared smooth class; the quadratic graph forms and the curl/div expressions are computed with the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. The rectangular assertions are the recorded $G2$ content of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]]: the reflection parities convert the boundary class into a rectangular torus class, the imported one-dimensional complete trigonometric system and Hilbert Fourier expansion give product completeness, and the finite-dimensional Fourier ODE with conservation of $\varepsilon|\hat E|^2+|\hat B|^2/\mu$ gives the unique weak solution and energy conservation; the direct TE/TM mode verification is the recorded physics branch G1 on the guide page and is not a mathematical dependency here. The recorded K10 branch (uniform Ohmic loss) is a physical-model branch of the same modal argument and is homed on the physical page, not here.

item.title: Gauge reachability: Lorenz gauge on the all-space slab and Coulomb gauge on a bounded smooth domain, with residual freedom
item.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and completed-expansion-arguments.md#W6; bounded-domain branch closed locally with the published elliptic resolvent and higher-order Dirichlet estimates; branch (b) parameter/ambient extension and compatible boundary-family estimates: physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-gauge-reachability-regularity-proposal.md
item.design_state: complete branch argument preserving the two Lorenz/Coulomb settings and restoring smooth parameter-dependent admissible Dirichlet/Neumann boundary data; incompatible data remain excluded
item.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in branch (a) and the Axiom of Choice together with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as declared by its weak-solvability lemmas in branch (b) ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $c>0$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of the framework ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ and Lorenz divergence $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$. (a) [All-space slab; Lorenz gauge] Let $t_0<T$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (the restriction of a $C^\infty$ pair on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; the transformed pair $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, has the same field pair $(E,B)$, and any two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. This is the exact content of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] read for potential pairs of the framework; its physical content is that every smooth potential representation of a field pair on a slab admits a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, without changing the fields. (b) [Bounded smooth domain; Coulomb gauge with admissible boundary families] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ graph domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an arbitrary interval, possibly unbounded, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be $C^\infty$ on an actual neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$. Prescribe either (i) a Dirichlet family $g_D(p,t)$ smooth in boundary charts on a neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega\times\overline I$, or (ii) an outward conormal family $\kappa(p,t)$ with the same smoothness and the compatibility $\int_{\Omega_j}\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)\,dS=0$ for every connected component $\Omega_j$ and every $t\in I$. Then there is a gauge generator $\psi$, the restriction of one $C^\infty$ function on an actual open neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$, such that $\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. In case (i), $\psi(p,t)=g_D(p,t)$ on $\partial\Omega\times I$, and its restriction to $\Omega\times I$ is unique with those Dirichlet values. In case (ii), $\varepsilon_0\partial_\nu\psi(p,t)=\kappa(p,t)$ there, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}\psi(\cdot,t)\,dx=0$ for every component and every $t$ gives a unique generator on $\Omega\times I$; without that normalization it is unique modulo smooth time-dependent spatial constants on each component. The transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge and has the same physical field pair ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Any two Coulomb-gauge generators differ by a function spatially harmonic at every $t$; equal Dirichlet data eliminate that residual freedom, whereas equal Neumann data leave only the componentwise constants just described. Zero Dirichlet data are the corresponding special case. Auxiliary ambient continuations away from the physical region need not be unique. (c) [Residual freedom on star-shaped domains] Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $(\varphi,A)$, $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ be two potential pairs of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-interval]]) with the same field pair, both in Lorenz gauge. If I is non-open, these C2 classes and the resulting generator use the open-neighbourhood restriction convention of lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials; for the physical open laboratory interval they have their ordinary C2 meaning. If a degenerate I is used in this branch, choose the ambient C2 extensions as part of the data: the same-field and Lorenz conditions refer to these extensions on an ambient time neighbourhood before restriction, and their time jets are not determined uniquely by the restricted values alone. Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^2$ jointly with $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)=T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ and $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. (d) [Scope] Nothing is asserted about gauge functions meeting arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions: in (a) the gauge function has zero Cauchy data at $t_0$ and no spatial boundary condition or decay, and $\Omega$ is all of $\mathbb R^3$; in (b) the datum is either a smooth time-dependent Dirichlet family or a smooth outward conormal family satisfying the stated componentwise compatibility at every physical time, with zero-mean normalization for Neumann uniqueness; the older promise of a global Lorenz gauge on a bounded domain with prescribed boundary data is explicitly outside this result. The Coulomb-gauge statement concerns the spatial divergence in the chosen inertial chart, and the instantaneous appearance of the Coulomb potential is a property of the representation, not a signal: only the field pair $(E,B)$ is physical content ([[def-em-fields]]).
item.strategy:
(a) is [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] with its hypotheses and countable choice carried verbatim; the pair of the framework enters only through the vocabulary, so nothing is reproved. (b) The fixed-time smooth Dirichlet and compatible Neumann interfaces are those of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]], and their parameter-compatible ambient smoothness, exact boundary lifts, complete natural-Neumann estimates and normalized uniqueness are supplied by the earlier pure-mathematical [[lem-em-parameter-dependent-smooth-poisson-boundary-solvers]]. Use the original open neighbourhood of the potentials and of the boundary family to choose an open time interval $J$ containing $\overline I$ by compactness of each fixed spatial/boundary fibre; only $\overline\Omega	imes K$, with compact $K\subset J$, is used for derivative bounds, never compactness of all $\overline I$. Put $F_t=\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)$. In the Dirichlet case the supplier constructs a fixed finite-chart spatial lift $H_t=L_Dg_D(\cdot,t)$ and the zero-trace operator $R$ for $-\varepsilon_0\Delta$ from its exact weak solver, including every $L^2$ source, with its higher-order bounds. Set $\psi_t=H_t+R(F_t+\varepsilon_0\Delta H_t)$. Differentiation includes the lift at every order: $\partial_t^j\psi_t=L_D\partial_t^jg_D+R(\partial_t^jF_t+\varepsilon_0\Delta L_D\partial_t^jg_D)$. Thus the spatial equation is $-\varepsilon_0\Delta\psi_t=F_t$ and the Dirichlet family is exact. In the Neumann case use the same supplier's compatible normalized weak solver and natural-boundary estimates. Compatibility is imposed only for $t\in I$: on an open $J$, define $c_j(t)=\int_{\Omega_j}F_t+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa_t$ and the auxiliary bulk extension $\widehat F_t=F_t-c_j(t)/|\Omega_j|$ on each of the finitely many components. It is smooth, compatible for all $t\in J$ and agrees with $F_t$ on $I$; no equation for the gauge outside the physical interval is promised. Apply the parameter solver to $(\widehat F,\kappa)$ with zero mean on each component. In either case locally uniform compact-time difference-quotient estimates give all mixed derivatives up to the boundary, and the supplier's fixed parameter-preserving Seeley construction supplies one actual ambient $C^\infty$ continuation, not merely separate finite-order Sobolev representatives. The resulting generator obeys $\Delta\psi=-\operatorname{div}A$ on every physical time, with the requested boundary data, so it is Coulomb gauge and preserves the fields by [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]. Elliptic uniqueness gives the stated normalized uniqueness on $\Omega	imes I$; subtracting any two Coulomb generators gives $\Delta\chi=0$ and the listed Dirichlet/Neumann residual freedom. This argument retains the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice hypotheses of the variational, chart and Sobolev suppliers, and imposes no global time bounds or extra regularity restriction. (c) Put $\delta\varphi=	ilde\varphi-\varphi$ and $\delta A=	ilde A-A$. Equality of the field pairs gives $\operatorname{curl}\delta A=0$ and $
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$. Apply the corrected scalar lemma to $C=\delta A$ and denote its negative-gradient witness by $\phi_{\delta A}(x,t)=-\int_0^1\langle\delta A(a+s(x-a),t),x-aangle ds$. Then $
abla\phi_{\delta A}=-\delta A$ and $\phi_{\delta A}$ is jointly $C^2$. Take $$\chi_0=-\phi_{\delta A}=\int_0^1\langle\delta A(a+s(x-a),t),x-aangle ds,$$ so $
abla\chi_0=\delta A$. This additional negation is essential; using the lemma's negative-gradient witness itself as the gauge generator would reverse the vector-potential difference. Mixed partials of the $C^2$ function $\chi_0$ now give $
abla(\delta\varphi+\partial_t\chi_0)=
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$. For fixed t, restrict this $C^1$ scalar to each radial segment $a+s(x-a)$; the chain rule gives zero derivative, and cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant gives its common value $h(t)=\delta\varphi(a,t)+\partial_t\chi_0(a,t)$. Since $\chi_0(a,t)=0$ for every t, the time derivative there is zero, so $h(t)=\delta\varphi(a,t)$ (in particular h is C1; indeed C2 under the stated hypotheses). For nondegenerate I, fix $t_*\in I$ and set $$\eta(t)=-\int_{t_*}^{t}h(u)du.$$ cor-primitives-of-a-continuous-function gives $\eta'=-h$ on I, with relative endpoint derivatives; since h is C1, eta is C2. Put $\chi=\chi_0+\eta$. Then $
abla\chi=\delta A$ and $\partial_t\chi=\partial_t\chi_0-h=-\delta\varphi$, so $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)$. Finally the unchanged exact gauge-shift identity in pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form(b) gives $0=G(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)=G(\varphi,A)-W\chi=-W\chi$, hence $W\chi=0$. The corrected radial construction gives chi0 as a C2 restriction from an open radial-admissibility neighbourhood. At the centre, the data extension gives h(t)=delta phi(a,t) on an open time neighbourhood; take the interval component containing I and construct the time primitive there. Adding this primitive to the chi0 extension yields a C2 extension on the intersection neighbourhood of Omega x I. Thus the asserted generator retains the same regularity convention at included endpoints of nondegenerate time intervals. Degenerate interval restrictions do not supply unique time jets: any use of this time-derivative branch there carries chosen ambient extensions and the same-field/Lorenz hypotheses on an ambient time neighbourhood, to which the nondegenerate construction applies before restriction. On an empty restriction there are no pointwise equations to prove. The physical laboratory branch already uses a nonempty open time interval.  This residual construction uses no choice principle; the preexisting Choice assumptions in branches (a)-(b) remain exactly as stated. The linearity of $
abla$ and $\partial_t$ used throughout is [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]; $H^m$ notation is [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and the elliptic problems use the domains of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. The declared Choice assumptions enter only through the elliptic existence theorem and the wave supplier and are carried in the statement. No claim beyond (a)-(c) is made.

item.title: Poincare inequality with mean subtraction on a bounded connected C-one domain
item.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (used through the smooth-up-to-the-boundary density theorem below) and the Axiom of Countable Choice (declared by the flattening and Sobolev suppliers). The axiom interfaces are [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded connected $C^1$ domain in the graph sense ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], [[def-connected-space]]); its closure is compact, so the boundary has a finite cover by boundary charts ([[def-compact-space]]). There is a constant $C_\Omega$, depending only on $\Omega$, with $$\|v-v_\Omega\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\,\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\qquad\text{for every }v\in H^1(\Omega),\qquad v_\Omega:=\frac1{|\Omega|}\int_\Omega v\,dx .$$ Here $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with the weak coordinate derivatives, and $\nabla v$ denotes the weak gradient. The estimate is the mean-zero (Poincare) inequality needed for weak Neumann solvability, where the mean-zero subspace carries the gradient norm.
item.strategy:
On a rectangular box $R$ the one-dimensional fundamental theorem along coordinate segments with Cauchy-Schwarz ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]) gives $\int_R\int_R|v(x)-v(y)|^2dx\,dy\le C_R|R|\int_R|
abla v|^2dx$; replacing $x$ by $y$ one coordinate at a time bounds the squared finite sum by three times the sum of the three one-coordinate differences, and Fubini-Tonelli ([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]) integrates the remaining coordinates. For almost every fixed $x$, write $v(x)-v_R=|R|^{-1}\int_R(v(x)-v(y))dy$. The $L^2$ Cauchy–Schwarz inequality ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]) gives $|v(x)-v_R|^2\le |R|^{-1}\int_R|v(x)-v(y)|^2dy$. Integrating in $x$ and using the preceding double-integral estimate gives $\int_R|v-v_R|^2\le C'_R\int_R|
abla v|^2$. This is an integral Cauchy–Schwarz argument, not an application of finite Jensen to a continuous average. The same argument applies to a half-box. Each boundary graph chart is flattened to a half-box; the $C^k$ boundary flattening lemma ([[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]]) transports the estimate to the chart patch, initially for smooth functions and then for $H^1$ functions by the smooth-up-to-the-boundary density theorem ([[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]]), with bounded chart Jacobians and first derivatives. Interior balls are replaced by boxes contained in $\Omega$. Compactness of the boundary and of the residual interior region gives a finite connected cover $\Omega= igcup_jU_j$ with every $|U_j|>0$ and a connected intersection graph: otherwise the finite disjoint unions of graph components would be nonempty relatively open sets partitioning the connected $\Omega$ ([[def-connected-space]]). Writing $a_j$ for the mean of $v$ on $U_j$, the local estimates give $\|v-a_j\|_{L^2(U_j)}\le C_j\|
abla v\|_{L^2(U_j)}$, and the mean differences $|a_j-a_k|$ over nonempty overlaps are bounded by the local gradient energy along a finite spanning tree of the intersection graph. Summing the local squared bounds and the squared mean differences over the finite cover, and using that the global mean minimises $a\mapsto\int_\Omega|v-a|^2$, gives the stated bound.

item.title: The L-two Dirichlet resolvent and smooth zero-boundary test density
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let `Omega` be a bounded `C∞` domain in `R3`, in the graph sense of `def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts`; connectedness is unnecessary. Write `H^m(Omega)=W^{m,2}(Omega;R)` with the multi-index integral norm and `H0^1(Omega)` for the `H1` closure of `Cc∞(Omega)`. For every real `f in L2(Omega)` there is a unique `u in H0^1(Omega) ∩ H2(Omega)` satisfying

$$\int_\Omega(\nabla u\cdot\nabla v+uv)=\int_\Omega fv\quad(v\in H_0^1(\Omega)).$$

It satisfies `(1−Delta)u=f` distributionally and almost everywhere as an `L2` identity, and

$$\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$

Moreover `D={phi in C∞(closure Omega): phi|boundary Omega=0}` is dense in `H2(Omega) ∩ H0^1(Omega)` in the `H2` norm: every such `w` has `phi_j in D` with `phi_j→w` in `H2`. Here smoothness on the closure means restriction of a smooth function in a neighbourhood of the closure, equivalently the smooth chart representatives used below. In particular, `grad phi_j→grad w` in the graph norm of `H(curl) ∩ H(div)`, with zero curl and `div grad w=Delta w`; every `grad phi_j` is smooth and PEC since its tangential derivatives vanish at the boundary. For precision, let `X_Omega` be the graph-norm closure of smooth vector fields on a neighbourhood of the closure with `nu cross v=0` on the boundary, where `nu` is the outward Euclidean unit normal. The ambient graph space consists of real `L2` vector fields whose distributional `div v=sum_i partial_i v_i` and `curl v=(partial_2 v_3-partial_3 v_2, partial_3 v_1-partial_1 v_3, partial_1 v_2-partial_2 v_1)` lie in `L2`; its norm squared is `||v||2^2+||curl v||2^2+||div v||2^2`. Thus `grad w` belongs to this explicitly defined `X_Omega`, the same completion used by the later cavity item. No equality with every maximal trace realisation is asserted.

No smoothness of `f`, no classical boundary value for general `u`, and no general nonsmooth-domain, Neumann, interface, or variable-coefficient claim is included. Zero boundary condition means membership in `H0^1`; the published trace theorem identifies its trace as zero.
item.strategy:
1. **Variational existence and its sharp H1 bound.** B1 supplies completeness and the Hilbert structure of `H0^1`. Equip it with the full quadratic `H1` norm and set `a(w,v)=integral(grad w·grad v+wv)`. Cauchy–Schwarz on the four-component `L2` tuple makes this a bounded symmetric form, and `a(v,v)=||v||H1²`, so the coercivity constant is exactly one. The functional `ell(v)=integral fv` has norm at most `||f||2` because `||v||2≤||v||H1`. Apply B2's explicit minimizing-sequence solver, with its declared Countable Choice covered by AC, to obtain the unique weak `H0^1` solution and `||u||H1≤||f||2`. Testing against compactly supported smooth functions gives the distributional equation. No Lax–Milgram result or unproved minimizer theorem is substituted. None of B1's numerical Poincaré constants is used.

2. **Charts and admissible tangential tests.** Cover the compact closure by finitely many interior patches and smooth graph patches. Shrink each patch twice, with compact support away from its artificial sides, and choose cutoffs equal to one on the inner patches. A graph flattening followed, if needed, by reversal of the last coordinate sends the domain side to `t>0`; smooth charts and inverse bounds through order two give bounded local `H1` and `H2` changes of variables. With `y=Phi(x)`, `J=|det D(Phi^{-1})|`, `U=u∘Phi^{-1}`, the local weak equation is

$$\int A_{ij}\partial_jU\partial_iV+cUV=\int FV,\qquad A=J(D\Phi)(D\Phi)^{\mathsf T},\quad c=J,\quad F=J(f\circ\Phi^{-1}).$$

All coefficients and first derivatives are bounded on the chosen patch, `A` is symmetric and uniformly positive, and `||F||2≤C||f||2` locally. The change-of-variables formula and weak chain rule justify these identities. A localized flattened `U` lies in `H0^1` of the half-space: take the sequence of `Cc∞(Omega)` functions defining the original `H0^1` membership, multiply by the patch cutoff, and pull back. These are smooth compactly supported functions on the open half-space and converge in `H1`; their supports need not have a uniform distance from its boundary. Hence tangential translations and smooth cutoffs preserve this closure. For `k=1,2`, `w_h=delta_h^k U` and `V=−delta_{−h}^k(eta² w_h)` are admissible tests, pulled back and extended by zero outside the chart. Use a larger preliminary localization equal to one on the quotient neighbourhood, so its cutoff never changes the original equation on the test support. Interior patches allow all three quotient directions. No normal quotient crosses the boundary.

3. **The L2-data estimate, with no differentiated datum.** Put `S=F−cU`, only in `L2`. Discrete integration by parts and the quotient product rule give the principal term

$$\int\eta^2 A_{ij}(y+he_k)\partial_jw_h\partial_iw_h\ge\alpha\|\eta\nabla w_h\|_2^2.$$

The exact remaining principal terms are `integral eta²(delta_h Aij)∂jU ∂iw_h` and `integral [Aij(y+h)∂jw_h+(delta_h Aij)∂jU](∂i eta²) w_h`. Thus their absolute sum is at most

$$C\bigl(\|U\|_{H^1}+\|w_h\|_2\bigr)\|\eta\nabla w_h\|_2+C\|U\|_{H^1}\|w_h\|_2.$$

Here `||delta_h A||infinity≤||∂k A||infinity`, and the published directional increment estimate yields `||w_h||2≤C||U||H1` on the required enlarged quotient neighbourhood. The undifferentiated right side obeys

$$\left|\int S\,\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2w_h)\right|\le C\|S\|_2\bigl(\|\eta\nabla w_h\|_2+\|w_h\|_2\bigr),$$

because the same increment bound applies to `eta²w_h` in that direction. Cauchy–Schwarz and Young's inequality absorb half the principal gradient square and give, uniformly for all sufficiently small nonzero `h`,

$$\|\eta\nabla\delta_h^kU\|_2\le C(\|F\|_2+\|U\|_{H^1}).$$

This estimates the actual `L2` datum, not its difference quotient; no `delta_h F` or derivative of `f` is present. The published tangential-test lemma supplies the exact commutator identity, but this explicit estimate is still part of the new proof.

4. **Weak mixed derivatives and corrected normal recovery.** On a smaller patch where `eta=1`, for every compactly supported smooth test `psi`, discrete integration by parts gives `integral delta_h^k(∂jU) psi = −integral ∂jU delta_{−h}^k psi`, whose limit is `−integral ∂jU ∂k psi`. The uniform bound in step 3 makes this distribution a bounded functional in the `L2` norm on tests. Extend it continuously to the closed `L2` subspace generated by those tests, which is Hilbert by `L2` completeness; Riesz gives an `L2` representing function with the same bound. This represents `∂k∂j U` distributionally. No weakly convergent subsequence, reflexivity theorem, or asserted density of tests in the whole `L2` space is required. Thus boundary patches have every second derivative with at least one tangential index; weak derivatives commute by testing smooth functions. The divergence-form equation gives the missing normal derivative with the signs

$$A_{33}\partial_{33}U=cU-F-\sum_{(i,j)\ne(3,3)}A_{ij}\partial_{ij}U-\sum_{i,j}(\partial_iA_{ij})\partial_jU.$$

Every term on the right is in `L2` and `A33≥alpha>0`, so division yields `∂33U in L2` and its bound. This follows distributionally before making the almost-everywhere identification. Interior patches already have all second derivatives. Return through the bounded `H2` chart maps, sum the finitely many inner-patch estimates, and obtain `||u||H2≤C(||f||2+||u||H1)≤C_Omega||f||2`. The equation now holds in `L2`. Uniqueness in `H0^1∩H2` is already uniqueness in the larger variational space.

5. **Zero-trace H2 density: prerequisites and flat gluing.** This step applies to every `w in H2∩H0^1`, not just the resolvent. Use a finite smooth ambient partition with one interior part and boundary parts compactly contained in graph charts. Multiplication and flattening preserve `H2`; a boundary part gives a compactly supported `W in H2(H)` with flat trace zero by chart compatibility and bounded trace continuity (or by the `H0^1` approximating sequence from step 2). Its support is separated from the chart's artificial edges. To justify the reflection, first obtain unrestricted smooth `H2` approximants of `W` on the half-space from the published `k=2,p=2` half-space extension, multiplication by a fixed compact cutoff equal to one on its support, and whole-space mollification. They converge in `H2`, so traces of the functions and their first derivatives converge in `L2` by the published `H1` flat trace bound. For any `zeta in Cc∞(R2)` and tangential `k`, their classical boundary integration by parts gives `integral T(∂kW) zeta = −integral TW ∂k zeta = 0`. Hence `T(∂kW)=0` as a distribution and almost everywhere; uniqueness of regular distributions follows directly from mollification/test pairings. This proves the needed tangential trace identity, rather than assuming it.

Define the odd reflection `W_o(y,t)=W(y,t)` for `t>0`, `−W(y,−t)` for `t<0`. A piecewise `H1` function whose two traces agree is globally `H1`: prove this by testing each half against a compact smooth ambient test, using smooth half-space approximation, one-variable integration and Fubini; the sole interface contribution is the difference of its two traces and hence cancels. Apply this gluing calculation first to `W_o` (both traces zero), then to its first derivatives. The tangential derivatives are odd reflections of `∂kW`, with both traces zero by the preceding argument. The normal derivative is the even reflection of `∂tW`, with identical traces on both sides; its trace need not vanish. Thus `W_o in H2(R3)`, and each derivative has the indicated reflected `L2` class; its `H2` norm is `sqrt(2)||W||H2`. No delta layer occurs. Even reflection of `W`, or zero extension in `H2`, would generally fail and is not used.

6. **Mollification, localization, and the actual cavity norm.** Choose a real compactly supported mass-one mollifier invariant under `t→−t`, for example a radial one, and convolve `W_o`. The mollifications converge in `H2(R3)` because weak derivatives commute with convolution and the `L2` approximate identity converges for each of the finitely many derivatives. They remain odd, so vanish exactly at `t=0`. Multiply by a fixed smooth cutoff in the flattened ambient chart equal to one near the support of `W_o`, with support separated from the artificial edges. This preserves boundary vanishing and convergence. For all sufficiently small radii the cutoff may also be chosen even in `t`, although only zero values at `t=0` are needed after multiplication. Pull back through the smooth chart and extend by zero outside its artificial support to get globally smooth functions on a neighbourhood of the closure with zero physical boundary value. Approximate the interior part by compactly supported smooth functions using legitimate compact-support zero extension and mollification, with radii smaller than its distance from the physical boundary. Add the finitely many parts, choosing radii tending to zero (AC covers sequence choices), to obtain `phi_j→w` in `H2` with `phi_j|boundary=0`. Each lies in `H0^1` by the published zero-trace kernel theorem. Finally `curl grad phi_j=0`, `div grad phi_j=Delta phi_j`, and `n×grad phi_j=0`, the last identity following by differentiating the identically zero smooth boundary restriction. Therefore

$$\|\nabla\phi_j-\nabla w\|_2+\|\operatorname{curl}(\nabla\phi_j-\nabla w)\|_2+\|\operatorname{div}(\nabla\phi_j-\nabla w)\|_2\longrightarrow0.$$

The curls vanish distributionally by commutation of weak derivatives, which is a direct test-function calculation. This is exactly convergence in G3's graph norm, giving `grad w in X` without a maximal-trace-density assumption.

item.title: Weak Neumann and transmission existence with interface charges
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the actually cited Sobolev trace, lift and mean-zero density interfaces, and its Countable Choice consequence for the measure and variational interfaces ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $\varepsilon$ be measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic, let $ho\in L^2(\Omega)$, and let $g\in H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$, the bounded real dual of the boundary trace space ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]). Define $\ell(v)=\int_\Omegaho v+\langle g,Tvangle$ on $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]). A weak Neumann solution is a $u\in H^1$ with $$\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\ell(v)\qquad	ext{for every }v\in H^1(\Omega).$$ Such a solution exists if and only if $\ell(1)=0$, and is then unique up to an additive constant; normalising $\int_\Omega u=0$ makes it unique. On finitely many connected components the compatibility and normalisation are imposed separately on each component. For finitely many disjoint smooth stationary interfaces with piecewise smooth uniformly elliptic $\varepsilon$, bulk data $ho\in L^2$ and prescribed sheet charge $\sigma$ on the interfaces defining a bounded trace functional on $H^1$ (for instance $\sigma\in L^2$ of each smooth compact interface), the same argument gives weak Dirichlet or compatible Neumann existence for the transmission problem, with the globally $H^1$ potential having identical one-sided trace; where the solution is classically smooth on each side, integration by parts gives the jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$, equivalently $n\cdot[D]=\sigma$ for the explicitly defined mathematical flux $D:=-\varepsilon
abla u$ on each side. General piecewise classical regularity remains a separate requirement.
item.strategy:
Full AC is inherited from [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] and [[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]]; the symmetric minimising-sequence solver itself needs only Countable Choice. No stronger choice principle is used. The trace bound of the prescribed-data lemma and Holder's inequality make $|\ell(v)|\le C\|v\|_{H^1}$ ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]). Testing the equation with $v=1$ makes $\ell(1)=0$ necessary. The mean-zero subspace of $H^1$ is closed, and the mean-zero coercivity lemma makes its gradient norm equivalent to the complete $H^1$ norm ([[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]]); the symmetric coercive variational solver ([[lem-em-symmetric-coercive-variational-solver]]) solves the coercive symmetric form there. Every $v\in H^1$ is its mean-zero part plus a constant, and the constant term contributes zero on both sides by compatibility, so this solves the full problem; for the difference of two solutions tested against itself the gradient vanishes, and the mean-zero inequality makes the difference constant. Each finite disjoint component is treated separately. The transmission case replaces $\ell$ by the sum of the bulk, boundary and interface trace functionals of the prescribed sheet charge; the same variational argument applies, and the one-sided trace identity holds for the globally $H^1$ potential by trace continuity in each chart, giving the stated jump relation where the solution is classically smooth on each side. In the classical jump equivalence define $D:=-\varepsilon
abla u$ piecewise; then $[D]=-[\varepsilon
abla u]$, so $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ is exactly $n\cdot[D]=\sigma$. Here $D$ is a mathematical flux vector, not an undeclared physical displacement field.

item.title: A fixed smooth-domain extension that preserves smooth parameters
item.statement:
Let `Omega⊂R3` be a bounded smooth graph domain. Choose an open spatial neighbourhood `V` of its compact closure. There exists a fixed real linear spatial extension operator `E_Omega`, determined only by the domain, finite charts and cutoffs, with this parameter property. For every open interval `J` and function `u:Omega×J→R` that is smooth in the interior and whose every mixed derivative has a continuous extension to `closure Omega × J`, the function `E_Omega u` is `C∞` on `R3×J`, equals `u` and all its continuous boundary jets on `closure Omega × J`, and is supported spatially in one fixed compact subset of `V`. For every compact `K⊂J`, integer `m≥0` and `j≥0`,

$$\sup_{t\in K}\|\partial_t^j E_\Omega u(\cdot,t)\|_{C^m(\mathbb R^3)}\le C_m\sup_{t\in K}\|\partial_t^j u(\cdot,t)\|_{C^m(\overline\Omega)}.$$

The `C^m` seminorm is the finite sum of suprema of spatial derivatives through order `m`. The extension commutes with every time derivative; charts and coefficients do not depend on `t`. No uniform bound over all of an unbounded `J` is assumed. Vector-valued inputs of finite dimension are extended componentwise. This construction adds no choice principle: a finite atlas can be selected from the cover of all admissible chart patches, finite cutoffs are supplied by the published finite-partition/cutoff lemmas, and the infinite coefficient sequence is defined explicitly below. The consuming elliptic/Sobolev argument retains its already-declared AC assumptions.
item.strategy:
**1. Explicit coefficients; no unproved moment lemma.** Put `b_k=−2^k`, `k=0,1,...`. For `N≥k` define

$$a_k^{(N)}=\prod_{\substack{0\le j\le N\\j\ne k}}\frac{1-b_j}{b_k-b_j},\qquad a_k=\lim_{N\to\infty}a_k^{(N)}.$$

The factors for `j<k` have sign negative, those for `j>k` positive; the sign is `(-1)^k`. For every finite index set, `prod(1+2^{-j})≤6`: the factors `j=0,1` give 3, and for the tail `j≥2`, the sum of `2^{-j}` is at most `1/2`, while the elementary induction `prod(1+x_j)≤1/(1−sum x_j)` bounds that tail by 2. Similarly `prod_{l=1}^M(1−2^{-l})≥1/4`: separate the first factor `1/2`, and use `prod(1−x_j)≥1−sum x_j≥1/2` on `l≥2`. The geometric-series supplier gives the stated sums, including their starting indices.

For `j<k` the absolute product is

$$2^{-k(k+1)/2}\frac{\prod_{j<k}(1+2^{-j})}{\prod_{l=1}^{k}(1-2^{-l})};$$

for `j>k` it is `prod_{j=k+1}^N(1+2^{-j})/prod_{l=1}^{N-k}(1−2^{-l})`. Thus

$$|a_k^{(N)}|\le576\,2^{-k(k+1)/2}\qquad(N\ge k).$$

At fixed `k`, the positive absolute value increases with `N`, since every new tail factor is greater than one, and it is bounded by this displayed constant. The published real monotone convergence theorem gives the limit `a_k`, with the same bound and sign. This defines every coefficient without selecting unspecified sequences.

For each integer `r≥0`, finite interpolation gives `sum_{k=0}^N a_k^{(N)} b_k^r=1` when `N≥r`: the polynomial

$$z^r-\sum_{k=0}^N b_k^r\prod_{\substack{0\le j\le N\\j\ne k}}\frac{z-b_j}{b_k-b_j}$$

has degree at most `N` and vanishes at the `N+1` distinct nodes `b_0,...,b_N`, so is zero by the exact published real-polynomial root bound; evaluate at `z=1`. To pass to the limit, the bound above gives `|a_k^{(N)} b_k^r|≤576·2^{-k(k+1)/2+kr}` uniformly in `N`. For `k≥2r+1` this is at most `576·2^{-k}`, whose tail tends to zero. First cut the sum at a fixed `M`, pass to the limit in those finitely many coefficients, and then let `M` increase. This proves both

$$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k b_k^r=1,\qquad\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|a_k|\,|b_k|^r<\infty\quad(r\ge0).$$

No original Seeley coefficient existence assertion is used as an unproved prerequisite.

**2. One flattened patch, with arbitrary parameters.** Write a smooth boundary patch as `(y,s)`, `s>0` inside the domain. A localized input `w(y,s,t)` has spatial support compactly inside the ambient chart, separated from its artificial edges, and every mixed derivative extends continuously to `s=0`. Extend it by zero at the artificial positive-side edges to the half-space. Choose a fixed smooth real normal cutoff `rho` that equals 1 near 0 and vanishes for `s≥delta/2`, with `delta` small enough that all sampled positive collar points remain in the chart. Define

$$\mathcal Ew(y,s,t)=w(y,s,t)\ (s\ge0),\qquad\mathcal Ew(y,s,t)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k\rho(b_ks)w(y,b_ks,t)\ (s<0).$$

For fixed negative `s`, the sum is locally finite because `b_k s=2^k|s|` eventually exceeds the cutoff support. It is therefore smooth off `s=0`. For any normal order `r`, tangential multi-index `alpha`, time order `j`, and compact parameter/tangential set, its termwise derivative for `s<0` is

$$a_k b_k^r\,[\partial_z^r\partial_y^\alpha\partial_t^j(\rho(z)w(y,z,t))]_{z=b_ks}.$$

On the fixed compact collar and a compact `K⊂J`, every input derivative in this formula is bounded; the supremum of the sum is bounded by a finite cutoff-dependent constant times `sum|a_k||b_k|^r`. The bounds hold locally uniformly up to `s=0`, with the **same** compact time set `K`; only the normal spatial argument is sampled.

As `s↑0`, for each fixed term the normal cutoff is identically one and all its positive-order derivatives vanish. The derivative therefore tends to `a_k b_k^r partial_s^r partial_y^alpha partial_t^j w(y,0,t)`. The finite-head/uniform-tail argument using the weighted absolute sum proves uniform convergence of the boundary limit on compact `(y,t)` sets. The moment identity then makes that limit exactly the input boundary derivative. This establishes matching continuous derivatives of every mixed order; no derivative of an infinite nonuniformly convergent series is assumed at the boundary.

**3. Matching jets imply actual joint smoothness.** For a function glued from the two sides, matching values give continuity. If the side first partial derivatives extend continuously and agree, the normal coordinate-segment FTC, on either side and up to `s=0`, proves the derivative at `s=0` equals their common limit. For tangential or time segments at `s=0`, first write the coordinate-segment FTC at `s≠0`, then let `s→0`; uniform convergence on the compact segment passes the integral to the common continuous boundary derivative. FTC again gives that tangential/time derivative on `s=0`. Thus the glued function is `C1` jointly. Apply the same argument successively to the already-matched derivatives of orders 1,2,... to obtain `C∞` on the ambient patch × `J`. The input itself obeys those boundary segment identities by the same limit from its positive side. This is a complete smooth-gluing argument, not a reference to a Whitney extension theorem.

The derivative bound at total spatial order `m` uses only input derivatives through `m`, with `sum|a_k|2^{km}` finite and the fixed cutoff derivatives through `m`. The operator is linear and does not change the time argument, so the time-commutation identity and the stated local seminorm estimate follow.

**4. Finite chart gluing on the fixed smooth domain.** Choose finitely many shrunk smooth graph charts and an interior open patch. Compactness gives finitely many smaller balls covering the domain closure, with their closed larger balls contained in the assigned chart/interior open members. Using the choice-free Euclidean compact cutoff supplier, take smooth nonnegative psi_l equal to one on each smaller ball and supported in its larger ball. S=sum_l psi_l is positive on a neighbourhood of the closure. Choose a smooth outer cutoff chi equal to one near the closure and compactly supported in {S>0}. For each chart j set chi_j=chi(sum of psi_l assigned to j)/S on {S>0}, and zero elsewhere. These functions are smooth, have supports in the chart members, and sum to one near the closure. Only finitely many choices are made; no measure-convention partition theorem is used. Localize u by these fixed spatial cutoffs. The interior piece is supported away from the physical boundary and is extended by zero, preserving smoothness. Each boundary piece is pulled through its smooth chart and extended by the preceding formula. Choose a fixed outer chart cutoff equal to one on both the positive localized support and the small negative support created by the extension, with compact support inside the larger chart; multiply before pulling back. This makes each piece smooth across its artificial edges when extended by zero in ambient space. Such collar sizes and cutoffs are available by shrinking the finite compact patches. The extension's tangential support never leaves that of the localized piece, and its negative normal support stays within `|s|<delta/2`, so the claimed outer support control is genuine.

Pullback is smooth by repeated ordinary chain rule with chart derivatives bounded at each fixed order on those compact supports. Add the finitely many pieces. On the domain their sum is `u` by the partition identity; all boundary jets agree by continuity from the interior. Each support lies in a fixed compact subset of the prescribed `V`, so their finite union does too. The charts, partitions and coefficient sequence are independent of time. This proves the claimed single parameter-preserving operator and its `C^m` seminorm bounds; it introduces no temporal patch choices or global bounds on unbounded intervals.

item.title: Smooth parameter-dependent Dirichlet and compatible Neumann Poisson solvers
item.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice carried by the variational/Sobolev suppliers. Let `Omega` be a bounded smooth graph domain in `R3`, `epsilon>0` constant and `J` an open interval. Let the bulk datum `f` be jointly smooth up to `closure Omega×J` in the all-mixed-derivative sense of the first supplier, and let boundary families `g_D`, `kappa` be smooth in a fixed finite boundary atlas × `J`. Then the Dirichlet problem `−epsilon Delta u=f`, `u|boundary=g_D` has a unique solution on `Omega×J`; it has a single smooth ambient continuation near the closed spatial domain × `J`. The Neumann problem `−epsilon Delta u=f`, `epsilon partial_nu u=kappa` has such a solution precisely when

$$\int_{\Omega_j}f(\cdot,t)+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)=0\quad\text{for each component and every }t\in J.$$

It is unique modulo a separately chosen spatial constant on each component at each time. The normalization `integral_Omega_j u(·,t)=0` gives a unique smooth family. Both solution operations are linear in their data; time differentiation commutes with them. Smoothness and estimates are local in compact time subintervals, with no uniform-in-`J` requirement. The smooth ambient continuations are auxiliary and are not unique off the closed physical spatial region.
item.strategy:
**Fixed boundary lifts.** Use a finite boundary partition, graph coordinates `r=x3−h(y)`, with the domain on `r<0`, outward normal `nu=(-grad h,1)/sqrt(1+|grad h|²)`, and a fixed normal cutoff equal to one near 0. On a localized boundary datum `g_j(y,t)`, the Dirichlet lift is `rho(r)g_j(y,t)` with a larger fixed chart cutoff. For an outward conormal datum `kappa_j`, the Neumann lift is

$$L_N\kappa_j(y,r,t)=\frac{r\rho(r)\kappa_j(y,t)}{\epsilon\sqrt{1+|\nabla h(y)|^2}},$$

again with a fixed larger chart cutoff equal to one near the datum support. At `r=0`, the terms from differentiating the coefficient or cutoff vanish because of the factor `r`, while `partial_nu r=sqrt(1+|grad h|²)`; hence `epsilon partial_nu L_N kappa_j=kappa_j`. Add the finite chart pieces. The partition's boundary sum is one, so both lifts have the exact required datum. They are linear, independent of time, smooth in an actual spatial collar × `J`, and their spatial `H^{k+2}` norms are bounded by constants times finite `C^{k+2}` boundary seminorms. Choosing higher seminorm orders is allowed; no sharp boundary Sobolev norm is asserted. For Dirichlet, subtract the lift and apply the earlier zero-lift weak Dirichlet solver plus the exact published higher-order Dirichlet estimate to the source `f+epsilon Delta L_Dg_D`.

**Neumann weak existence and H1 bound.** The earlier weak Neumann lemma accepts the bulk `L2` datum and the bounded boundary trace functional, and proves necessity/sufficiency of componentwise compatibility. Smooth boundary `kappa` defines that bounded functional by Cauchy–Schwarz and the exact published `H1→L2(boundary)` trace theorem. Mean-zero coercivity on each component gives

$$\|u\|_{H^1}\le C_{\Omega,\epsilon}\bigl(\|f\|_2+\|\kappa\|_{L^2(\partial\Omega)}\bigr)$$

for the normalized solution, by testing against it and absorbing the gradient norm. A bounded smooth graph domain has only finitely many components: every bounded open component has boundary in the domain boundary; a finite cover by connected one-sided graph patches meets only finitely many components, and every component meets such a patch. Thus all normalizations and lift/estimate sums are finite. After subtracting `H=L_N kappa`, the residual `w=u−H` has homogeneous Neumann flux and source `f+epsilon Delta H`; its mean is the negative mean of `H`. The smooth first Green identity verifies the weak lift subtraction, and the divergence theorem verifies that its residual bulk integral is zero under the original compatibility. A constant normalization does not affect the flux or elliptic equation.

**Natural-boundary H2 estimate; explicit source terms.** Flatten the fixed smooth boundary and take a localized weak solution `z∈H1` supported away from artificial chart edges, whose weak equation, for supported `H1` tests including nonzero boundary trace, is

$$\int A_{ij}\partial_jz\partial_iv=\int p v+\int G_i\partial_iv,\quad p\in L^2,\ G\in H^1.$$

The smooth symmetric uniformly positive transformed `A` is the ordinary Jacobian/metric transform of the constant scalar operator. The original homogeneous-flux problem has `G=0`; localization by a spatial cutoff `eta` changes the scalar datum to `eta p−A grad z·grad eta+G·grad eta` and the vector datum to `eta G+z A grad eta`, still respectively `L2` and `H1`. These exact terms account for natural flux under localization; no false zero-trace condition is imposed.

For a tangential direction `k`, put `w_h=delta_h^k z` and test with `v=−delta_{−h}^k(eta² w_h)`. This is a supported `H1` test, allowed by the natural variational formulation; it need not vanish at the physical boundary. The published quotient integration-by-parts/product/weak-commutation identities give principal term `integral eta² A(y+h) grad w_h·grad w_h≥alpha||eta grad w_h||²`. item.title: Classical elliptic regularity on smooth domains and across smooth interfaces
item.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice inherited from the stated weak-existence, Sobolev extension and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive, and let $\rho$ be smooth on the closure. Prescribe in the prescribed-data lemma either smooth Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$, or smooth outward flux data $g$ with its compatibility condition as in the weak Neumann lemma. Then the weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ with those data is $C^\infty$ on the closure $\overline\Omega$. For finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, the weak solution is smooth on each closed side. Edge and junction points, reentrant corners and coefficient loss of regularity are excluded. The existence claims are those of the two weak solvability lemmas; this lemma proves their classical upgrade on the declared domains.
item.strategy:
The existence claims use the AC-qualified prescribed Dirichlet and weak Neumann suppliers; that assumption is transported explicitly rather than inferred from the word "weak solution". Local estimate. In an interior patch, or in a flattened smooth boundary/interface patch, write the weak equation in divergence form $\int a_{ij}\partial_ju\,\partial_iv=\int fv+\int G_i\partial_iv$ with the transformed coefficients $	ilde a=|\det D\Phi^{-1}|\,D\Phi\,a\,D\Phi^{\mathsf T}$; positivity of the Jacobian bounds and the bounds on $D\Phi$ preserve uniform ellipticity. Dirichlet data are removed by subtracting the smooth lift $g(y)\eta(t)$ built from a finite subordinate smooth partition and a normal cutoff; smooth Neumann flux is converted to smooth volume data by a collar vector field $G$ with $G\cdot n=g$ and the divergence theorem. For a tangential direction $k$, put $w:=\delta_h^ku$, and take a cutoff $\eta$ supported in a smaller patch; test the weak identity with $v=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2w)$; change of variables and the product identity give the principal bound $\alpha\|\eta
abla w\|_2^2$ against cutoff terms $C\|u\|_{H^1}[\|\eta
abla w\|_2+\|w\|_2]$, the crucial increment estimates $\|\delta_hu\|_{L^2}\le\|\partial_ku\|_{L^2}$ (from the ACL line identity $\delta_h^ku=\int_0^1\partial_ku(x+	heta he_k)d	heta$, $L^2$ Cauchy–Schwarz on the unit $	heta$ interval and Fubini; the derivative norm is taken on the larger patch containing the shifted segments) and $\|\delta_ha\|_\infty\le\|\partial_ka\|_\infty$, and $f,G$ terms; Cauchy-Schwarz and $2AB\le(\alpha/2)A^2+2B^2/\alpha$ ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]) absorb the gradient terms, giving uniform difference-quotient bounds. The weak second derivatives that are purely tangential (or mixed interior) exist through the bounded functional obtained by passing to the limit of the difference quotients; the Hilbert Riesz representation ([[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]]) supplies an $L^2$ representative, with no pointwise derivative or weak subsequence selection. With compactly supported tests the weak identity is $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f-\operatorname{div}G$ distributionally. Expanding that divergence, at a boundary or interface the normal second derivative is recovered from $a_{33}\partial_{33}u=\operatorname{div}G-f-\sum_{(i,j)
e(3,3)}a_{ij}\partial_{ij}u-\sum_{ij}(\partial_ia_{ij})\partial_ju$ with $a_{33}\ge\alpha>0$. A finite cover of the compact closure gives global $H^2$ bounds on each declared side. The higher-order induction differentiates the weak equation by tangential multi-indices; the exact coefficient commutator is finite and $H^1$, so the same local estimate raises the regularity by two orders of tangential/mixed derivatives, and the normal-recovery equation raises the remaining normal counts one by one; Dirichlet tangential derivatives keep zero trace and natural tests stay admissible. Classical representative: the Sobolev extension theorem ([[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]) extends each piecewise $H^m$ class to a compactly supported $H^m(\mathbb R^3)$ function, and the Fourier characterisation of integer-order Sobolev spaces ([[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]) with Fourier inversion ([[thm-l-two-fourier-inversion]]) converts $W^{m,2}$ membership with $m>j+3/2$ into a $C^j$ representative via the absolutely convergent inverse integral. Derivatives agree with the weak ones by testing and Fubini, representatives agree by continuity, and arbitrarily large $m$ gives a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure whose continuous trace is the prescribed one. Existence of the weak solutions is supplied by the prescribed-data and weak-Neumann lemmas ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]).

item.title: Spectral completeness of the curl operator in a smooth PEC cavity
item.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, as used by the complete variational, Sobolev-extension and compact-spectral suppliers. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain. Define $H(\operatorname{curl})=\{u\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{curl}u\in L^2\}$ and $H(\operatorname{div})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{div}u\in L^2\}$ with their graph norms, and let $X$ be the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$; this is an explicit weak perfect-electric-conductor boundary class. Put $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline{V}^{\,L^2}$. Then the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity tending to infinity whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and the zero eigenspace is finite dimensional and must be retained when the topology allows it. The eigen equation is $$\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$$ distributionally with the PEC trace, and for the associated second-order wave with initial displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$ the coefficients solve $a_j''+c^2\lambda_ja_j=0$, with convergence in $C_tV\cap C_tH$ for finite-energy data and the finitely many $\lambda=0$ modes linear in time. No identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation, and no lossy, open or non-smooth-domain spectral claim, is made.
item.strategy:
Compactness and $H^1$ equivalence. For smooth $u$ with $n	imes u=0$, expanding $|\operatorname{curl}u|^2$ and integrating once gives $\int_\Omega(|\operatorname{curl}u|^2+|\operatorname{div}u|^2-|
abla u|^2)=\int_{\partial\Omega}(\operatorname{div}n)|u\cdot n|^2dS$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] and the divergence theorem on the collar). The curvature is bounded on the compact smooth boundary, and the collar normal-line identity $|u(y,0)|^2=|u(y,t)|^2-\int_0^t\partial_s|u|^2ds$ with $2ab\le\delta a^2+\delta^{-1}b^2$ gives $\|u\|_{L^2(\partial\Omega)}^2\le\delta\|
abla u\|_2^2+C_\delta\|u\|_2^2$; absorbing the curvature term yields $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|u\|_2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_2+\|\operatorname{div}u\|_2)$, so the completion $X$ is a closed $H^1$ subspace with zero tangential trace by trace continuity. The $H^1$ inclusion in $L^2$ is compact by the elementary cube-averaging proof using the bounded smooth-domain extension ([[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]): for a bounded family of extensions the rectangular mean estimate gives uniform $\|u-P_hu\|_2\le Ch\|
abla u\|_2$ with $P_h$ of finite-dimensional range, so a finite $\varepsilon$-net exists in total bounded and complete $L^2$. The shifted form $a(u,v)=\int[\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v+\operatorname{div}u\operatorname{div}v+u\cdot v]$ is coercive and complete, so the symmetric solver ([[lem-em-symmetric-coercive-variational-solver]]) defines $K_0$; if $f$ is distributionally divergence-free and $q=\operatorname{div}K_0f$, testing with $v=
abla\varphi$ gives $\int q(\Delta\varphi-\varphi)=0$ for all smooth zero-trace $\varphi$, and the local Dirichlet resolvent and smooth-zero-boundary test-density lemma ([[lem-em-dirichlet-resolvent-h-two-and-smooth-test-density]]) gives the unique $\varphi\in H^2\cap H_0^1$ solving $(1-\Delta)\varphi=q$. Its smooth zero-boundary approximants $\varphi_j$ converge in $H^2$, so $
abla\varphi_j$ are smooth PEC fields converging to $
abla\varphi$ in the curl/div graph norm, proving this gradient belongs to the chosen completion $X$. The identity for smooth $\varphi_j$ passes by $L^2$ continuity to $\int q(\Delta\varphi-\varphi)=-\|q\|_2^2=0$; hence $K=K_0|_H$ maps $H$ into $V$ and is bounded $H	o V$ and compact $H	o H$ ([[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Testing its defining equations with $Kg,Kf$ proves self-adjointness, and $(f,Kf)=\|\operatorname{curl}Kf\|^2+\|Kf\|^2>0$ for $f
e0$ proves trivial kernel. The compact self-adjoint spectral theorem ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators]]) now gives an orthonormal eigenbasis of $H$ with positive eigenvalues $\kappa_j	o0$ of finite multiplicity; substituting $Ku_j=\kappa_ju_j$ into the full $X$ identity gives $\int\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=(\kappa_j^{-1}-1)\int u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, and testing with compactly supported $v$ gives $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ distributionally with $\lambda_j=\kappa_j^{-1}-1\ge0$, the zero eigenspace being finite dimensional by the spectral theorem. The wave statement is the standard coefficient decomposition $a_j''+c^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with finite-sum energy convergence, exactly as in the rectangular case, retaining the finitely many $\lambda=0$ linear modes.

item.title: Well-posed weak solvability and classical regularity for declared smooth-domain elliptic boundary problems
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the weak-solvability lemmas. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] is the local graph definition used throughout), let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive ($\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le eta|\xi|^2$ on $\Omega$ for some $0<\alpha\le eta<\infty$), and let $ho$ be smooth on $\overline\Omega$. Then:
(a) **Dirichlet.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one weak solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $g$ of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$; it depends continuously on the data, is $C^\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$, and satisfies $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ pointwise with $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$.
(b) **Neumann.** For every smooth outward conormal datum $g$ satisfying $\int_{\Omega_j}ho\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g\,dS=0$ on every connected component $\Omega_j$ of $\Omega$, there is a weak solution of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$. It is unique up to a separately chosen additive constant on each component, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ for each component gives a unique normalised solution, smooth on each closed component. In particular on a connected domain the compatibility is $\int_{\partial\Omega}g=-\int_\Omegaho$, with a single additive constant.
(c) **Transmission.** For the stated finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth uniformly positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth bulk $ho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, prescribe either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum of (a), or the smooth outer Neumann datum of (b). The weak right-hand side includes $\int_\Omegaho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$ and, in the Neumann case, $\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$. With outer Dirichlet data the globally $H^1$ solution is unique. With outer Neumann data it exists exactly when the total right-hand side vanishes on the constant of each connected component, equivalently $\int_{\Omega_j}ho+\sum_{\Gamma\subset\Omega_j}\int_\Gamma\sigma+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$ for each $j$, and is unique modulo componentwise constants; zero componentwise means give uniqueness. In either case the equal one-sided traces and $C^\infty$ regularity on each closed side hold, and the flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ in the sign convention of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]].
Edge and junction points, reentrant corners, coefficient loss of regularity and general piecewise classical regularity beyond finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces are excluded. The existence content is that of the two weak solvability lemmas; this item states the combined existence-and-regularity theorem on the declared domains.
item.strategy: The claim collects three recorded branches and their compatibility. (a) Existence, uniqueness, exact prescribed trace and continuous dependence are [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]; the classical upgrade to $C^\infty$ on the closure, with the classical equation and boundary values, is [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (b) Testing the displayed weak identity with the constant on each component gives $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$, including the minus sign when solved for the outer conormal integral. Necessity of componentwise compatibility, existence, uniqueness modulo componentwise constants and the normalised form are [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; the classical upgrade is again [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (c) Apply the transmission functional including the sheet-charge term, with outer Dirichlet tests in $H_0^1$ for full uniqueness, or outer Neumann tests in $H^1$ with that functional zero on every componentwise constant and the chosen mean normalisation. The weak existence and the one-sided trace identity are the transmission part of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], the two-sided classical smoothness and the jump relation are [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]], and the passage from the weak identity to the interface flux uses the divergence theorem for the piecewise smooth configuration together with the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. The smooth coefficients, conormal field and chart changes are smooth by the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]; the inner products and the quadratic form $\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u$ use the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No existence or regularity claim is made beyond the stated smooth-domain, finite-interface regime.
